review_type: single AI curator; full final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: confirms the band is a direct product of the target gene (not an indirect effect of the KO).
errors.issue: Untagged rescue can restore a downstream cross-reactive protein; this does not distinguish direct antigen identity from indirect dependence.

errors.quote: the signal is lost if, and only if, the cognate gene is ablated.
errors.issue: The supplied one-way perturbation does not establish an if-and-only-if relationship.

errors.quote: identifies the cross-reactive species and closes the assignment gap.
errors.issue: A gel region can contain multiple proteins; peptide identification supplies candidate identities, not automatic assignment of the immunoreactive antigen.

rationale: Correctly selects 50 kDa and acknowledges indirect effects, but its decisive proposed rescue interpretation contradicts that caveat. Mass-spectrometry and competition interpretations are also overconfident. These errors materially impair the requested discrimination.
reference_guardrails: Comparable loading does not establish antigen identity or guarantee equivalent transfer of each species.
No expected target molecular mass is supplied. Do not assume 50 kDa is the predicted full-length mass.
Untagged rescue may restore either the target or an indirectly dependent antigen.
Gel-slice proteomics and native immunoprecipitation can contain co-migrating proteins or partners; identity of a constituent is not automatically identity of the immunoreactive species.
No requirement to mention private draft status or obsolete multiple-choice distractors.
Complete coding deletion blocks new target synthesis; pre-existing protein and signal mixtures are possible caveats when timing and turnover are unspecified, not established explanations.
A reference list of methods does not make any single validation approach infallible.
